Parents forced teen daughter to live in the woods because she ate a Pop-Tart.
Whilst it does seem like unnecessary punishment, I'm not sure that making your kid live in a tent for a week constitutes child abuse. What does everyone else think?

I think it absolutely does. She was only 14. The article mentions that the area she was left in has a large wild hog population so I'm assuming that makes it pretty dangerous. It also mentions some weird process of her having to pick up food from some person in a specific location at a specific time each day.
So they fed and housed her, just in pretty weird conditions. It seems like an asshole thing to do, but I'm not sure how it's breaking the law.

I'm not sure a tent in the woods counts as housing her especially considering the wild hog population. If she encountered a wild hog or another wild animal she could have easily died.

If you wanted to go camping with your daughter that's one thing but they left her alone. Not sure what the laws for child abuse are but in my opinion this sounds like it should count.

IDK, seems a bit sketchy to me. Do parents who let their kids take part in extreme sports get prosecuted if they injure themselves? The world is a dangerous place.

I'm not saying those parents aren't reprehensible idiots, just that the law might be overstepping its boundaries in this case.

If kids want to do activities like participating in extreme sports, they're voluntarily putting themselves in dangerous situations. Forcing your child to survive out in the woods for 7 days is not voluntary.

I just don't see the logic. I'm not a parent, but I'm also not crazy. The header image of the parents shows me that they're more interested in themselves than raising a child, especially a teenage daughter.

My ideal solution, I suppose, is something like.. "You know, we pay a lot of attention to ourselves and are forcing our ideals on a kid that doesn't agree. We should spend more time with our kid. We should take her camping for a week while she's on summer break instead of letting her sit inside eating garbage."

I get the counterpoint @EliCash is trying to make. And certainly, it doesn't strike me as the most awful thing I've read today (there is also the headline of boy beaten to death for stealing a slice of cake) but its certainly an odd form of punishment. As a parent, it's simply not something I would be able to do. I don't think essentially shunning or excommunicating a family member is the best method of conflict resolution.
